statements.statement: PLOS ONE's editors issued an Expression of Concern because of unresolved issues, and the authors did not respond or could not be reached.
Apparent vertical discontinuity in Figure 4's LSD1 blot between 293T and A549 lanes.
The paper uses this figure to show LSD1 is lower in A549 than H460, which is how it chose A549 for over-expression and H460 for siRNA.
Figure 7 contains no LSD1 siRNA data, so the reported reduction in H460 migration is not supported.
Controls in the transfection experiments are not described well enough to replicate.
Similarities with other groups' work call into question validity and provenance.
The notice does not retract the paper or give corrected results; findings in doubt but not withdrawn.
Section 3 cites Lv et al. [12] for reduced H460 migration after LSD1 siRNA in scratch assay and takes it as the clearest indication LSD1 drives migration.
Notice says Figure 7 has no siRNA data, so this use is touched.
Section 2 cites Lv et al. [12] for higher LSD1 in tumour in 80 NSCLC patients and shorter survival association.
The notice questions validity and provenance generally but does not specifically name the patient tissue or survival findings; unclear whether touched.
The notice is an EoC about unresolved issues, authors did not respond, no retraction; impact medium.
Section 3 cites Lv et al. [12] for reduced H460 migration after siRNA and takes it as clearest indication, but the notice says Figure 7 has no siRNA data so the reduction is not supported.
